question: Which of the following drugs used in the treatment of female infertility is an analogue of the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) capable of inhibiting gonadal steroidogenesis during continued treatment ?:
analysis: Buserelin is a GnRH analogue that, when used continuously, suppresses gonadotropin release, leading to decreased gonadal steroidogenesis. This mechanism is utilized in the treatment of female infertility to control hormone levels. Clomiphene is a selective estrogen receptor modulator, Cetrorelix is a GnRH antagonist, and Progesterone is a hormone, none of which function as GnRH analogues to inhibit steroidogenesis.
